The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(N=2100\). For each prime \(p\), a move replaces the two \(p\)-exponents of the chosen numbers by their minimum and maximum, so the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

At the end, every possible move leaves the board unchanged. A move on \(a,b\) leaves the board unchanged exactly when
\[
\{a,b\}=\{\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\},
\]
which happens iff \(a\mid b\) or \(b\mid a\). Thus the final board is a divisibility chain.

List the final numbers as
\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]
Since divisibility implies numerical order, the \(2026\)th smallest number is \(x_{2026}\).

For a fixed prime \(p\), the exponents \(v_p(x_i)\) are nondecreasing, and their multiset is the same as initially. Hence the number of \(i\) with \(v_p(x_i)\ge t\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor.
\]
The \(2026\)th smallest number is the \(75\)th largest number, so
\[
v_p(x_{2026})=\max\{t:\lfloor 2100/p^t\rfloor\ge 75\}.
\]
Since \(2100/75=28\), this is the largest \(t\) with \(p^t\le 28\).

Thus:
\[
v_2=4,\quad v_3=3,\quad v_5=2,
\]
and
\[
v_p=1 \quad\text{for } p=7,11,13,17,19,23,
\]
while all other primes have exponent \(0\).

So
\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]
Its number of divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6=5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot64=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
